overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 18
overview.text: In this lesson, students continue to construct residual plots. Residual plots are analyzed to determine if the points are scattered at random around the horizontal line (indicating a linear relationship) or if the points have a pattern (indicating a nonlinear relationship).
outcomes: Students use a graphing calculator to construct the residual plot for a given data set.
Students use a residual plot as an indication of whether the model used to describe the relationship between two numerical variables is an appropriate choice.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.

vocabulary.definition: Why does the first scatter plot result in an arch shape in the residual plot? The points in the scatter plot are not in a straight line.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 18 Exit Ticket: Analyzing Residuals
exitTicket.prompt:
Exit Ticket

If you see a clear curve in the residual plot, what does this say about the original data set?

If you see a random scatter of points in the residual plot, what does this say about the original data set?
exitTicket.solution:
If you see a clear curve in the residual plot, what does this say about the original data set?

A clear curve in the residual plot shows that the variables in the original data set have a nonlinear relationship.

If you see a random scatter of points in the residual plot, what does this say about the original data set?

A random scatter of points in the residual plot shows that a straight line is an appropriate model for the relationship between the two variables in the original data set.

problems.prompt:
For each of the following residual plots, what conclusion would you reach about the relationship between the variables in the original data set? Indicate whether the values would be better represented by a linear or a nonlinear relationship.

Suppose that after fitting a line, a data set produces the residual plot shown below.

An incomplete scatter plot of the original data set is shown below. The least squares line is shown, but the points in the scatter plot have been erased. Estimate the locations of the original points, and create an approximation of the scatter plot below.
problems.solution: This problem should challenge students. There are many correct answers. Students should show points in the scatter plot whose vertical deviations from the given least squares line are in proportion to the values of the residuals in the residual plot. A student's answer is only acceptable if it shows a general pattern like the one shown above. Confirm that each student's points could result in (approximately) the given least squares line.
